description: MUN International Press alumni with strong skills in journalism, content writing, and policy research. I specialize in climate advocacy and data storytelling—translating complex NASA data into high-impact narratives. Looking for developers, UI/UX designers, or teams working on Earth Science/Climate challenges to collaborate. I can lead our project research, presentation, and press management.
summary:
Earth System Trend Detective is a free web tool that turns students into data detectives. Users pick a case file (global temperature, atmospheric CO₂, sea level, or the Antarctic ozone hole) or upload their own regional time series from NASA Giovanni. A continent picker gives the bounding box to paste into Giovanni for Africa, Asia, Australia and Oceania, Europe, the Americas or Antarctica.

The tool plots the time series, with optional seasonal-cycle removal and yearly averaging, and answers four questions: what is changing, where, by how much per decade, and whether the change is statistically significant. It fits a least-squares trend with a 95% confidence interval, then runs a t-test, the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s robust slope. It also adjusts for autocorrelation and warns when a straight line may not fit.

Plain-language definitions, a guided demo and a presentation mode make it usable by high school students and the public. Understanding whether a change is real or random is the foundation of climate science.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective is a web tool that helps students and the public find out whether a change in the Earth system is real. The user picks a case file (global temperature, atmospheric CO₂, sea level or the Antarctic ozone hole) or uploads a regional time series from NASA Giovanni. A continent picker gives the bounding box to paste into Giovanni for Africa, Asia, Australia and Oceania, Europe, the Americas or Antarctica.

The tool plots the series, with optional seasonal-cycle removal and yearly averaging, then answers what is changing, where, by how much per decade, and whether the change is statistically significant. It fits a least-squares trend with a 95% confidence interval and runs a t-test, the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s robust slope. It also adjusts for autocorrelation and warns when a straight line may not fit or the window is too short.

Plain-language definitions, a guided demo, a presentation mode, downloads and a responsive layout make it usable from phones to projectors. Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the statistics written from scratch and checked against scipy. Limits: only straight-line trends are tested, and the built-in data are snapshots saved on November 14, 2026.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI): Select the options for code and for text (and for data, if listed). Don’t select images, video or audio, because the project contains none. I already put an AI note in the About section and in the page’s metadata, which the form asks for.
